NDT training in Casper, WY: how it works for Casper employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Casper technicians and employers is self-paced online theory with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, followed by hands-on practice in person at the employer's own shop or field site. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Casper. The courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and your Casper employer certifies you. We reply within one business day.

Casper has been an energy centre for more than a century, and that history shows in the number of service companies, fabricators and pipeline contractors based in and around it. Central Wyoming mixes oil and gas, refining, power generation, mining and wind development, and that variety means a technician with a good grounding in NDT is not tied to a single commodity.

Wyoming's distances and weather also shape the work. Crews drive long distances to sites on open plains, and winter conditions affect both inspection technique and scheduling. A training plan that lets theory be completed whenever the weather or the job allows, with the practical done at the employer's own site, is a good fit for that pattern.

Request a Casper training quote, and tell us the methods, levels and head-count you have in mind. In Casper, anyone planning ahead can also read the NDT training FAQ, the Atlantis training overview and the USA training page.

How to get NDT certified in Casper: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Certification in Wyoming follows the same pattern as elsewhere in the United States. In Casper, under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies its own technicians, and the standard is a set of recommended practices that each employer turns into a written practice of its own. Here is the sequence in order.

  1. Find or have an employer with a written practice. A technician in Casper is certified by the company that employs them, so the first step is a sponsor whose written practice covers the method and level you want. In Casper, the practice sets the hours, the examinations and the recertification interval.
  2. In Casper, complete the formal training. Take the classroom hours the written practice requires. The training-requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours for each method, and your Casper employer may set higher figures.
  3. Log supervised experience. Document the hours a Casper technician spends performing the method under a certified Level II or III. Experience is usually the slowest part for a new Casper technician, so start the log from the first day on a job.
  4. In Casper, pass the general examination on principles, equipment and terminology for the method.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the procedures, equipment and acceptance standards your Casper employer really uses.
  6. In Casper, pass the practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or a qualified examiner working under one.
  7. In Casper, pass the vision examination: near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation at the intervals the written practice sets. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker shows what to expect.
  8. Receive certification signed by your Casper employer.
  9. In Casper, recertify at the interval the written practice sets, which SNT-TC-1A recommends should not exceed five years, by examination or documented performance as permitted.

In Casper, ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, and ASNT NDT Level III examinations) is the alternative if you want a credential that stays with you rather than with an employer. Atlantis prepares candidates for that route too. See ASNT certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Casper technicians

In Casper, each course follows the body of knowledge in SNT-TC-1A for its method. In Casper, level 1 courses cover the fundamentals and working under supervision, Level 2 courses cover setting up, calibrating, performing and evaluating examinations to a procedure, and Level 3 preparation covers the basic and method examinations for those who will write procedures and examine others.

Method What the course covers Where it is used around Casper
UT Sound physics, calibration, thickness gauging, angle-beam weld examination, reporting Wall-loss surveys on tanks, vessels and piping; weld checks on new construction
RT In Casper, exposure technique, image quality, film and digital interpretation, radiation safety basics Pipeline and plant welds where radiography is specified
MT Magnetising methods, field direction, particle application, indication evaluation Structural welds, tower and crane components, drilling and lifting equipment
PT Process control, dwell times, surface preparation, indication interpretation Stainless and alloy piping, repair welds, small-bore connections
VT Acuity and lighting, weld profile, discontinuities, measuring tools, reporting First examination on pipeline, plant, tower and fabrication welds
PAUT In Casper, focal laws, encoded scanning, data analysis, sizing (UT Level II first) Pipeline welds and corrosion mapping where the operator permits phased array
TOFD Diffraction technique, setup, flaw sizing (UT Level II first) Thick-wall welds in refinery and power equipment

In Casper, PAUT and TOFD are advanced ultrasonic techniques and are generally taken after UT Level II. In Casper, whether they can be used on a given job depends on the customer's specification and the employer's written practice.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Casper

Ultrasonic testing is the method Casper technicians use for wall-thickness monitoring and for examining welds below the surface. A Level I course covers sound physics, equipment set-up, calibration and thickness gauging, and Level II adds angle-beam weld examination, evaluation against the acceptance standard, and reporting. In central Wyoming, thickness work on tanks, separators, refinery piping and boiler equipment is common, and weld examination follows pipeline and plant construction.

Cold weather matters: couplant behaviour, equipment batteries and surface condition all change in winter, and experienced technicians plan for it. The Practical NDT simulator lets you rehearse set-ups and scanning patterns indoors, while the ultrasonic testing training page lists the course content, and the UT Level 2 practice questions help you test the theory.

Where NDT technicians work around Casper

Oil and gas production and services. Casper is a base for operators and the service companies that support drilling and production across the Powder River Basin and other Wyoming plays. Contractors there are regularly asked for qualification records by operators.

Refining and pipelines. Wyoming has several refineries and a network of crude, products and natural gas pipelines, some of them running through central Wyoming. In-service inspection follows API 510, 570 and 653 for pressure equipment and PHMSA rules for pipelines, and some employers expect those inspector certifications separately from NDT method certification.

Power generation. Wyoming produces a large share of the country's coal and supports coal-fired generation, including plants in Natrona County and elsewhere. Boilers, turbines and pressure parts need outage inspection to ASME requirements. The state also has a growing wind generation sector, and tower and foundation weld inspection falls to AWS D1.1-based visual and magnetic particle work.

Uranium and mining. Wyoming is a significant uranium recovery state, and mining and processing operations rely on documented inspection of tanks, piping and structures. Nuclear-related quality requirements may add to a general SNT-TC-1A programme, and the employer sets those.

Fabrication and oilfield equipment. Casper has welding shops and equipment builders serving drilling, mining and construction customers, and they are often required to show customers inspector qualification records.

For earnings information on Casper-area work, see our NDT salary guide, which cites public sources. Energy employment is cyclical, and a technician with several methods and current certifications has more room to move.

NDT schools and classes near Casper: what to compare

People who search for NDT schools or classes in Casper will find colleges with welding and industrial programmes, private training companies, and employers with in-house training. Some run classroom courses on fixed timetables, and others offer self-paced theory. A classroom helps someone without an employer who wants time on specimens before applying for work. Self-paced theory helps someone who is already employed in the field, or a company that wants to qualify crews without long absences.

Ask each provider the same questions. Does the school certify you, or does your employer under a written practice? Will your prospective employer accept the training hours? In Casper, who writes and grades the practical examination, and is that person a Level III? Operator audits of contractors read the written practice and the technician's file, so a course that fits neatly into that paperwork is worth more than one that only produces a certificate.

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Casper. We provide online theory with Level III Q&A, the Practical NDT simulator for rehearsal, and onsite practical examination at an employer's facility. Our near-me guide explains how to approach employers about sponsorship.

Training a crew at your Casper facility

A Casper contractor with several technicians to qualify can run the complete programme at its own pace: self-paced online theory so crews stay on the job, then specific and practical examinations at your shop on your equipment and representative welds and piping. The specific examination can be built around the operator specifications and acceptance criteria your crews apply in the field.

If your written practice needs revision before an operator audit, our Level III can review it. See written practice development and corporate NDT training, or ask about training a Casper crew.

For Casper candidates the practical examination is hands-on with real equipment and specimens and is never conducted remotely. In Casper, if you want help writing the Level III side of the programme, see outsourced Level III consulting.

Radiography licensing in Wyoming

Radiography licensing in Wyoming needs careful checking. Wyoming joined the NRC's Agreement State programme in 2018, but my understanding is that the agreement is limited in scope and centred on uranium recovery, so the Nuclear Regulatory Commission may still license industrial radiography sources there. Confirm with the NRC and the Wyoming Department of Environmental Quality which agency licenses the source and the radiographers for a given job before mobilising. Whoever the regulator is, radiographers must meet the training and supervision conditions of the company licence. An RT method course does not license anyone or authorise use of a source. Wyoming employers normally need both radiation safety authorisation and SNT-TC-1A certification covering technique and interpretation.

Practise before your practical exam

The Practical NDT browser simulator lets a Casper technician rehearse set-ups, scanning coverage and interpretation in virtual workplaces between hands-on sessions, and the NDT practice tests cover the general and method theory. They are rehearsal tools. They do not replace hands-on training, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens under your Casper employer's written practice.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Casper

How do I get NDT certified in Casper?

Work for, or be sponsored by, an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the training and experience it requires, pass the general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and the employer certifies you.

Is there NDT work in Casper?

Yes, across oil and gas, refining, pipelines, power generation, uranium, wind and fabrication. Activity is cyclical, so ask operators and contractors directly about current needs.

Can I take NDT classes online in Wyoming?

Yes, the theory is self-paced online with Level III Q&A. In Casper, practical training and the practical examination are done hands-on with an employer.

Which NDT method should I learn first in central Wyoming?

Visual inspection with magnetic particle or ultrasonic thickness is a common start. Many technicians add radiography and penetrant testing.

How long does Level 2 training take?

The employer's written practice sets the hours. The training-requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended hours; experience usually takes the longest.

Does cold weather affect NDT?

Yes. Cold changes couplant behaviour, equipment performance and surface condition, and penetrant testing has temperature limits. Procedures should state them, and technicians should be trained to follow them.

Can I get Level III training in Casper?

In Casper, yes, preparation is online and self-paced with Level III Q&A. See ASNT Level III training.

Does a course certify me?

No. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies. In Casper, ASNT central certification is the alternative if you want a credential not tied to one employer.
